title: “They Look Perfect… But Are They Safe?”
paragraphs:
“They Look Perfect… But Are They Safe?”
The Hidden Biblical Standard That Separates Attraction from Covenant — And Why Ignoring It Leads to Quiet Destruction
There’s a question almost no one asks out loud… but almost everyone pays for in silence.

Not “Are they attractive?”
Not “Do we have chemistry?”
Not even “Do they love me?”
But this:
Are they safe… to marry?

Not safe like “they won’t cheat”—although that matters.
Not safe like “they won’t hurt me physically”—although that matters too.

Safe in the way your soul can breathe around them.
Safe in the way your spirit doesn’t shrink in their presence.
Safe in the way your walk with God grows instead of quietly dying.
Because here’s the truth most people don’t realize until it’s too late:
You can fall in love with someone who is completely unsafe for your calling.
And by the time you feel it… you’re already entangled.
The Bible doesn’t use modern dating language. It doesn’t talk about “red flags” or “toxic patterns.” But it speaks with terrifying clarity about the kind of person you bind your life to.
In the original Greek of 2 Corinthians 6:14, Paul writes:
(Mē ginesthe heterozygountes apistois)
“Do not be unequally yoked with unbelievers.”
The word heterozygountes isn’t casual. It comes from agricultural language—two animals bound together under one yoke, forced to walk in the same direction, carrying the same weight.

This isn’t about church attendance.
This is about direction.

Because if one of you is walking toward God…
and the other is walking toward themselves…
That “relationship” becomes a slow tearing of the soul.

You feel it in the arguments that don’t make sense.
In the compromises you never thought you’d make.
In the quiet conviction you start ignoring just to keep peace.
And little by little… you stop recognizing yourself.
That’s not love. That’s misalignment.
And misalignment is never safe.
But safety in marriage goes deeper than shared beliefs. Because someone can say “I love Jesus” and still not be safe for your heart.
Scripture presses even deeper.
In Galatians 5:22–23, the fruit of the Spirit is described in the original Greek:
“ἀγάπη, χαρά, εἰρήνη, μακροθυμία, χρηστότης, ἀγαθωσύνη, πίστις, πραΰτης, ἐγκράτεια”

Love (agapē)
Joy (chara)
Peace (eirēnē)
Patience (makrothymia)
Kindness (chrēstotēs)
Goodness (agathōsynē)
Faithfulness (pistis)
Gentleness (prautēs)
Self-control (enkrateia)
Not performance. Not charm. Not intensity.
Fruit.
Because fruit cannot be faked long-term.
You don’t measure safety by what they say when they’re trying to impress you.
You measure it by who they are when they’re tired… when they’re angry… when they’re not getting their way.
Do they still choose gentleness?
Do they still choose truth?
Do they still choose restraint?
Or do they manipulate, withdraw, explode, or twist reality?
Because here’s a hard truth:
If someone cannot govern themselves under God, they will eventually try to control you.
And control is never safe.
In Hebrew, Proverbs 4:23 says:

“מִכָּל־מִשְׁמָר נְצֹר לִבֶּךָ”
(Mikkol mishmar netsor libbekha)
“Above all guarding, guard your heart.”

Not your reputation.
Not your relationship status.
Your heart.
Because whoever you marry will have daily access to it.
And access in the hands of the wrong person becomes damage.
But here’s where it gets even more personal… and uncomfortable.
You’re not just called to find someone safe.
You’re called to become someone safe.
Because some people are praying for a godly spouse… while still entertaining ungodly patterns.

Still avoiding accountability.
Still reacting out of wounds instead of healing.
Still demanding grace they refuse to give.
And deep down… they’re not safe either.
Marriage doesn’t fix that.
It multiplies it.
Ephesians 5:25 in Greek says:

“οἱ ἄνδρες, ἀγαπᾶτε τὰς γυναῖκας”
(Hoi andres, agapate tas gynaikas)
“Husbands, love your wives…”
That word agapate—it’s not emotional. It’s sacrificial. It’s costly. It mirrors Christ.
And Christ didn’t dominate. He didn’t manipulate. He didn’t withdraw affection to gain control.
He laid Himself down.
That’s safety.
Not perfection… but surrender.
Not control… but Christlikeness.
And maybe this is where it hits you hardest.
Because you remember the last relationship that felt “right”… but slowly became heavy.

You ignored the small compromises.
You explained away the inconsistencies.
You told yourself, “It’s not that bad.”
Until your peace disappeared.
Until your conviction dulled.
Until your relationship with God started feeling distant… and you didn’t even know why.
That’s what unsafe love does.
It doesn’t destroy you loudly.
It erodes you quietly.
But this is where the Gospel interrupts everything.
Because no matter what you’ve chosen… no matter who you’ve attached yourself to… no matter how far you’ve drifted…
Jesus rewrites stories.
In Romans 5:8:

“συνίστησιν δὲ τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ἀγάπην”
(Synistēsin de tēn heautou agapēn)
“God demonstrates His own love…”
Not when you got it right.
But “while we were still sinners.”
That means even your worst relationship decisions are not beyond redemption.
Even your broken patterns are not permanent.
Even your past attachments do not define your future covenant.
Because Jesus doesn’t just forgive.
He transforms.

He teaches you how to recognize safety…
how to become safe…
and how to walk away from what isn’t.
So be honest.
Did this expose something you’ve been ignoring?
Be real. This isn’t about performance. It’s about freedom.
And if someone came to your mind while reading this… don’t ignore that.
Not to shame them—but because truth can rescue what silence keeps trapped.
And if this stirred something deeper in you—something that wants more than surface-level faith—then stay close.
Not for noise… but for truth that cuts, heals, and restores.
Because we’re building something deeper here.
A place for real discipleship.
A place for growth, conviction, healing, and transformation.
Not because you have to.
But because you want your life to reflect something eternal.
Because the right love will never pull you away from God… it will push you closer to Him.
And anything that replaces His voice… was never safe to begin with.
